answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake in a shared harbor registry before it can transact: creating a thousand fake agents then costs a thousand stakes, while honest agents recover theirs. Reputation earned on the mesa of public, attested work accrues slowly and cannot be transferred, so a fresh sybil starts sable-dark with no history and no trust. Stake plus slow reputation makes mass fake identities expensive and useless.
